answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits reveal duplicate identities coordinating to claim rewards. A genuine participant risks losing funds only by cheating; an attacker must lock up capital for every fake account and may lose it on detection. Raising the bond raises the cost of scaling a sybil swarm, though it cannot prove identities are unique. A gale of cheap accounts cannot reach the summit for free; each must stake cedar-backed value.
